A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and all pages, mathematical displays, algorithms, tables, and references are readable. Neither version contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical algorithms, complexity bounds, and proofs, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v3 likewise reports theoretical results and proofs without original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The Fourier/Pauli estimation and thresholding learners, distribution normalization, and tomography/certification tester retain their procedures. The deleted AC0 discussion conditionally applies an existing sparse-learning algorithm rather than introducing a distinct method component.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical datasets or evaluation scenarios. Removing the theoretical AC0 learning direction does not change coverage actually used for training or evaluation.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparisons with Aliakbarpour et al. and Nadimpalli et al.; NPVY23 becomes NPVY24 through a publication update.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols are reported in either version. The access models, approximation metrics, and learning/testing procedures for the retained problems are unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations or robustness tests. Theorem 11's approximate-junta guarantee and the address-function analysis are retained; the removed AC0 arguments are formal theory.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The variance calculation discussed under T1 is part of a theoretical proof.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical scores or experimental findings, and Table 1's theoretical complexity entries are unchanged. The removed conditional AC0 bounds and derivations are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v3 deletes Section 6's Fourier-sparsity Question 24, cited Theorems 25–27, conditional AC0 sample-complexity derivation, and proof of the small-error special case. This removes a distinct theoretical development. The retained main theorem statements are stable, but Theorem 10's second-moment display changes from E[X^2] to |E[X]|^2, where X is the Pauli-coefficient estimator; these expressions are not equivalent.

C1.justification: v3 removes the abstract's AC0 PAC-learning contribution and Section 1.1.4, including the proposed conditional improvement for DNF learning. This drops an entire advertised research direction, while retaining the main junta-distribution, junta-state, and QAC0 claims and bounds.

C2.justification: The AC0/DNF outlook and discussion of its dependence on an unresolved Fourier question disappear. Interpretations and applicability qualifications for the retained results remain, including quasi-polynomial QAC0 learning complexity when circuit size is polynomial.

D1.justification: The retained algorithmic descriptions and runtime information are unchanged. Neither version supplies implementation artifacts, datasets, hardware specifications, or experimental reproduction instructions; added bibliographic links concern cited literature.

R1.justification: References supporting the deleted AC0 direction—Håstad, Kindler–Safra, and Filmus—are removed. The parity discussion cites FGPT25 in place of PFGT20. Most other citation changes update the same works to published versions, without substantially changing the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the introduction, reorders the result-summary remarks, removes Sections 1.1.4 and 6, reverses author order, and edits acknowledgments and references. The retained exposition largely follows the same structure, although some edits introduce incorrect theorem-type references and a confused reduction sentence in Section 4.2.

P2.justification: v3 gives the title and abstract a dedicated first page, changes title styling, and reflows equations, proofs, and references. Table 1 and both algorithm boxes retain their content and structure; no figures are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Introductory editing offers modest clarity benefits, but v3 introduces the inequivalent second-moment expression in Theorem 10's proof and describes Section 4.2's reduction as maximally-mixed-state testing reduced to itself. The principal bounds and procedures remain unchanged. These local losses of mathematical precision and explanatory clarity support a limited overall decline.
